chapter: IX. The Persecution of the Church
title: [Measures against the Church in the Pyeng Yang Territory]
caption_extra: To sum up what has been committed against the Church in the Pyeng Yang territory by the police, gendarmes and soldiers, in line with the statements made above, we give the following: [Context, added by the transcriber: summary of the annual report (1918–19) of the American Presbyterian Mission Station at Pyeng Yang, quoted]

rows: They have arrested many of the leaders of the churches, including pastors, helpers, and school teachers. Many of the rest have fled for safety, for the Church leaders seem to have been singled out for punishment and persecution regardless of guilt or innocence.
They have seriously damaged nineteen church buildings and broken the bells in others.
They have expropriated the property of at least one Church for other purposes without asking for or receiving permission to use the same.
Twenty-six churches have been forced to close for periods up to three months and more.
Many church schools have been forced to close in both city and country, because of the arrest of teachers, for periods up to three months and more.
Helpers, pastors and Bible women have been ordered to stop preaching in many places.
Christian literature has been seized and destroyed in many places.
The police have ordered the non-Christians to drive the Christians out of their homes in several places.
All the students in the Union Christian College and the Boys' Academy in Pyeng Yang were ordered arrested by the Chief of Police whether guilty of any offense or not.
Christians have been discriminated against in many ways, of which the following are typical:
In the special severity shown Christians in connection with the spring " clean up."
In the frequency and severity of beatings administered by police in the performance of their official duties.
In the special effort to arrest and punish the leaders of the churches on the ground that they were per se leaders, too, in the independence movement.
Christian women in the country have been terrorized by police, gendarmes and soldiers.

The pastor of the Congregational Church for Koreans (under Japanese control), Mr. Takahashi, has visited certain of our churches and, assisted by police, has forced Christians to gather and listen to addresses intended to alienate them from the missionaries and their present church connection, and attempted to proselyte for his church. This was done with the knowledge and assistance of petty government officials.

transcriber_notes: Rows: 15 as printed (items 1–12; item 10 has sub-items (a)–(c) as rows 10 (a)–(c)). Table runs p. 171 (frame p0194) to p. 172 (frame p0195); owned here.
Figures are printed as words, kept as printed: 'nineteen' (item 2), 'Twenty-six' (item 4). Durations 'up to three months and more' (items 4, 5) are in the item text, not the figures column.

chapter: Appendix II. Treaties and Conventions Relating to Korean Independence
title: (c) Japan's Guarantee of Korean Independence
caption_extra: Excerpts from Treaties Made by Japan Recognizing or Asserting Independence of Korea:

rows: Chosen (Korea) being an independent State enjoys the same sovereign rights as does Japan.

The object of the alliance is to maintain the Independence of Korea on a firm footing. . . . Korea will undertake to give every possible facility to Japanese soldiers regarding their movement and supply of provisions. This Treaty shall cease and determine at the conclusion of a Treaty of Peace with China.
China recognizes definitely the full and complete independence and autonomy of Korea.

The Imperial Governments of Russia and Japan recognize definitely the Sovereignty and entire independence of Korea, and pledge themselves mutually to abstain from all direct interference in the internal affairs of that country.
The High Contracting Parties, having mutually recognized the independence of China and Korea, declare themselves to be entirely uninfluenced by any aggressive tendencies in either country.
The Imperial Government of Japan definitely guarantees the Independence and territorial integrity of the Korean Empire.
